about: OH's director script: the 16 beats as data the demo kit's director runs (public/demo-kit/director.js), scaffolded by scripts/demo-kit/new-demo.mjs from demo.config.json. Not a published beat document: those are beats/*.json, which scripts/demo-kit/seed.mjs re-anchors and the worker applies by name. Strings are templates over the facts oh.js computes (facts()); run lists are the kit's verbs; call is the one escape hatch into oh.js. A beat whose run is notBuilt says so on the status line and stops: its presses are its lane's to write.

beats.label: A stranger arrives from search
declare: Searches “{{arrival.term}}” and lands on the homepage ({{arrival.entry}})

{{#region.override}}Rehearsal override: region = {{region.override}} from the address bar (?region=), asserted and labelled{{/region.override}}{{^region.override}}The region comes from the request: the edge locates the visitor, and nothing is asserted{{/region.override}}
will: The hero and the deals answer the search and the visitor’s region: the campaign term seeds TV, that state’s sales lean the rest
Recommended for you and the TV grid lean with the sales of the visitor’s state on POST /sort, and say so: “leans with that state’s sales · synthetic → warehouse”

The Arrival panel names {{#region.override}}the override’s region, labelled as asserted{{/region.override}}{{^region.override}}the region the edge located, from the request{{/region.override}}, the census (shown, never scored) and the regional lean, labelled synthetic → warehouse
The visitor’s own meters are empty: nothing about them is known yet
beats.line: A stranger searches “{{arrival.term}}” and lands. The first paint answers the search and where they are: {{#region.override}}the region is a rehearsal override, labelled{{/region.override}}{{^region.override}}the region comes from the request{{/region.override}}{{#region.lean}}, and that state’s sales lean {{region.lean}}{{/region.lean}}. The census is shown, never scored; Compare sets the site’s own page beside it.

after.line: A stranger searches “{{arrival.term}}” and lands. The first paint answers the search and where they are: {{p1.arrival.sentence}}. Their own meters are empty; Compare sets the site’s own page beside it.

will: A different state’s lean on the same stranger: what leans on the region answers {{p1.contrastName || region.contrastName}}’s sales, and the page says which modules moved and which held
The Arrival panel and the rail’s label say the region is asserted, not observed; the visitor’s meters do not move
beats.line: The same stranger and the same page, in {{p1.contrastName || region.contrastName}}: asserted and labelled, never the opening default. Another state’s sales lean the page another way; the price is the same for everyone.

note: the contrast: asserted on the request, labelled · not observed

after.line: The same stranger and the same page, asserted in {{p1.contrastName || region.contrastName}}, never the opening default: {{p1.arrival.sentence}}. On this answer {{#p1.home.moved}}{{p1.home.moved}} moved{{/p1.home.moved}}{{^p1.home.moved}}nothing on the page moved{{/p1.home.moved}}{{#p1.home.held}} and {{p1.home.held}} held{{/p1.home.held}}{{#p1.home.lean}}; the rail {{p1.home.lean}}{{/p1.home.lean}}. The price is the same for everyone.

beats.label: Two TVs, then a washer

declare.text: Back in {{region.ownName}}, the visitor’s own region ({{#region.override}}the rehearsal override, labelled{{/region.override}}{{^region.override}}from the request, nothing asserted{{/region.override}})

declare: Opens the TV grid, the first TV it offers, then the next one
Opens the Laundry menu and the {{p1.washerName || 'front-load washer'}} page
Returns to the homepage
will: room and type rise on the shopper’s own meters: the living room and the laundry room, the TVs’ panel and a front-load

The room tiles reorder on the shopper’s rooms; the deals four hold both rooms by the slot’s own rule; Recommended for you asks POST /sort for each room’s four, then across the rooms, so it balances them instead of swapping wholesale
beats.line: The shopper opens two TVs, then a front-load washer, and the homepage changes with them, receipts behind every card: room and type rise, the room tiles reorder, the rail across rooms balances.

the TV grid shows no second TV to open

The step from one personalised module to a homepage that answers the shopper, on the platform LG already runs.

beats.label: The fresh visitor beside them
declare: Compare → Fresh visitor: the shopper’s homepage beside a stranger’s, asked in the same region with nothing sent
will: The shopper’s page and a fresh visitor’s, side by side: the same region’s prior and the same catalog; only what the visit earned is different
What changed sets the two answers behind the frames side by side, row by row
beats.line: Compare: the shopper’s page against a stranger’s in the same region. The same catalog and the same public prices; only what the shopper did is different.

beats.label: The washer page
declare: Opens the {{p2.washer.name}} page: through a link on screen when there is one, else from the address bar, as a shopper would
will: Below the buy box, which nobody decides: the dryer that goes with it, the pedestal and the stacking kit (the set price only when a set costs less than its pieces), each preferred because it completes {{p2.washer.sku}} (ctx.anchor), with the completes line on its receipt

Each card states its rule as our merchandiser’s and lists its products in POST /sort’s order, labelled with the sales of the shopper’s state, synthetic → warehouse; the dryer card says what led and why from /sort’s own drivers, and names the shopper’s fuel only when their profile holds one
beats.line: The washer page. Below the buy box, which nobody decides, the room completes: the dryer that goes with it, the pedestal and the stacking kit, each a merchandiser’s rule with its receipt.

after.line: The {{p2.washer.name}}: {{p2.onPage.completes}} modules complete it, each receipt reading “Completes what was committed to”: {{p2.onPage.completing}}.{{#p2.dryer.lead}} The dryer card leads with the {{p2.dryer.lead}}, by POST /sort’s own drivers: {{p2.dryer.why}}.{{/p2.dryer.lead}} The buy box above them is off limits, and says so.

beats.label: A switch to a top-loader
declare: Switches to a top-load washer with the page’s own type switch: {{p2.topLoader.name}}, the top-loader that sells best at this price
will: The pedestal leaves, and its card says why: a top-loader has no pedestal; the rule serves front-load pairs only, and the page now asserts ctx.family = top-load-washer
The before/now strip names what left and why; the dryer stays, completing the new washer
beats.line: The shopper switches to a top-loader and the pedestal leaves: a rule withdrawing itself, with its reason on the card.

after.line: The shopper switched to the {{p2.topLoader.name}}. Withdrawn by their own rule: {{p2.withdrawn}}. The card says why: {{p2.withdrawnWhy}}.

run.missing: no top-load switch on this page: the washer page (beat 5) carries it

will: The soundbar for its series and the mount for its VESA pattern, each completing {{p2.tv.sku}}, with the completes line on its receipt
beats.line: The TV page: the soundbar matched to its series and the mount for its VESA pattern. The same engine, a different room.

after.line: The {{p2.tv.name}}: {{p2.onPage.completes}} modules complete it, the soundbar from its series’ tier and the mount for its VESA pattern{{#p2.vesa}} ({{p2.vesa}} mm){{/p2.vesa}}. The same engine, a different room.

beats.label: The range page
declare: Opens the {{p2.range.name}} page

beats.line: The kitchen path: the range, the microwave above it, the dishwasher beside it, and the package when it costs less than the three.

after.line: The kitchen path on the {{p2.range.name}}: the microwave and the dishwasher that go with it, and {{p2.package.name}} at {{p2.package.price}}, {{p2.package.savings}} less than its pieces apart. The prices are the catalog’s.

beats.label: QNED beside OLED, a size up
declare: Opens the {{p2.qned.name}} page, with the OLED beside it
Says the shopper sits {{p2.distanceFt}} ft away, in the size-up tool: their answer, declared, carried as context on the next question (ctx.distance), never as a choice of theirs
Chooses the one size up with the card’s own button: the shopper’s own choice, sent as select
will: “For a bright room the QNED is the right choice; for a dark room this OLED is”, and the price is the same for everyone; nothing decided sits near the financing line
From the declared distance the card names one size up by its own rule; size band and price tier move on the shopper’s meters only once they choose it themselves
beats.line: A QNED page with the OLED beside it, and one size up from the declared viewing distance: when the shopper chooses it, tier and size band move. The price is the same for everyone, and nothing decided sits near the financing line.

after.line: The QNED, with {{p2.compare.other || 'the OLED'}} beside it: “for a bright room the QNED is the right choice; for a dark room this OLED is.” From {{p2.distanceFt}} ft, declared, the card names one size up, the {{p2.sizeUp.name}} at {{p2.sizeUp.price}}{{#p2.sizeUp.chosen}}; the shopper chose it themselves{{#p2.sizeUp.moved}}, and their own meters moved: {{p2.sizeUp.moved}}{{/p2.sizeUp.moved}}{{/p2.sizeUp.chosen}}. The price is the same for everyone.

run.missing: the engine did not decide the size-up module on this page, so there is nothing to press: the page never adds a module it was not given
the size-up card names no larger size here, so there is nothing to choose: the page never chooses for the shopper

beats.label: A closet width
declare: Opens the {{p2.washer.name}} page again
Enters the width of the laundry closet, {{p2.closet}} in: the shopper’s measurement, declared, never inferred
will: Models that do not fit drop out, and the page counts them: hidden, wider than your space; the next decision asserts ctx.fit, labelled declared
beats.line: The shopper enters the closet’s width, and the models that would not fit drop out, counted on the page: hidden, wider than your space.

after.line: The space is {{p2.fit.width}} in, declared: of the {{p2.fit.all}} {{p2.fit.kind}}, {{p2.fit.fits}} fit, and hidden: {{p2.fit.hidden}} wider than your space. The measurement is the shopper’s own, never inferred.

run.missing: no fit tool on this page: it needs a product of a kind the tool measures, with its width published

beats.label: An offer’s window closes
declare: Opens the {{p1.tvName || 'TV'}} page from the TV grid
Publishes the catalog: the gift-card offer’s window has closed, with the offers that close with it, on the homepage and on every TV page
Returns to the homepage: the packages with a member out of stock stay as the catalog publishes them, out of stock
will: On the TV page the closed offers leave on the next decision: the gift card goes from its offers

On the homepage the closed pieces can no longer be chosen, and a package with a member out of stock is never shown as complete: the page checks every answer and every recorded candidate of this visit for one
beats.line: The merchandiser’s day: an offer’s window closes. On the shopper’s TV page and on the homepage it leaves on the next decision, by the catalog’s own rules, and a package with a member out of stock is never shown as complete.

run.name: {{beatNames.windowCloses}}
run.reason: an offer’s window closes; a package member is out of stock
note: the gift-card offer and the offers that close with it, on the homepage and every TV page

after.line: The merchandiser’s day: {{#p1.windows.page}}on the {{p1.windows.pageName}} page {{p1.windows.page}} offers left with their windows on the next decision; {{/p1.windows.page}}{{p1.windows.closed}} offers’ windows closed in one publish{{#p1.windows.left}}, and {{p1.windows.left}} left the shopper’s homepage{{/p1.windows.left}}; {{#p1.windows.held}}{{p1.windows.held}} packages with a member out of stock were never shown as complete. {{/p1.windows.held}}By the catalog’s own rules, on every surface, at the next decision: windows and stock kept by the engine, the next step on the platform LG already runs.

Its receipt names what the engine would have led with, read off a ranked decision’s own receipt; the other three are still ranked for the shopper
beats.line: The merchandiser pins a launch series. The pin leads, and its receipt says so: the merchandiser outranks the engine, visibly.

note: container 1 of the deals for everyone · ranking skipped

after.line: The merchandiser pins {{p1.pin.title}}: container 1 for everyone, ranking skipped. Without the pin the engine would have led with {{p1.pin.would}}, container {{p1.pin.nowAt}} now: the merchandiser outranks the engine, visibly.

beats.label: Three weeks later
declare: Three weeks pass, labelled: every window moves back {{clock.days}} days in one publish. On the demo’s dial the shopper’s room signals are gone within minutes (production’s dial runs days: the published τ on room reads 60 days there)
The return visit is asserted on the homepage from now on (ctx.visit = return), labelled: the same browser, the engine’s own clock real
will: The shopper’s room signals fall below the entry threshold on the demo’s compressed dial: nothing of the rooms they browsed is left to lean the homepage
The continue hero answers the shopper’s return, resting on their shortlist (what they opened on this device, nothing inferred) and the decisions trail; its receipt says production’s dial is days
beats.line: Three weeks later, labelled as a clock jump: every window moves back {{clock.days}} days, and on the demo’s compressed dial the shopper’s room signals are gone within minutes, below the entry threshold (production runs days; the published τ would read 60 days there). The homepage picks up where they left off from their shortlist and the decisions trail.

beats.label: What changed in the meantime

The prices are the catalog’s, the same for everyone: they show as held unless the catalog’s own price moved
beats.line: What changed in the meantime: the offers on the shopper’s shortlist that ended and the ones still running, by the catalog’s own windows, and the prices, which are the catalog’s. The page says what changed; it never decides a price.

beats.label: The phone, then sign-in
declare: Signs in on the laptop as {{signIn.account}}, a fictional account: the worker mints the signed link{{#signIn.laptopLinked}} (signed in already: nothing to do){{/signIn.laptopLinked}}
Opens the site on the shopper’s phone: a second device, a stranger to the engine, with their own region’s opening
Signs in on the phone as {{signIn.account}}: the worker mints its link, and the page asks again
will: The phone’s first page is a stranger’s: the region and the catalog, nothing of the shopper’s
One request after its sign-in the same page answers with the laptop’s taste: the meters, the hero, the room tiles and the deals move
The receipt under the header reads “{{signIn.receipt}}”: linked at sign-in, with the shopper’s consent, never by matching devices
beats.line: On the phone the shopper is a stranger until they sign in as {{signIn.account}}: then the phone becomes the laptop’s taste in one request. Linked at sign-in and consented; no device matching.

beats.label: Best Buy counts
declare: Opens the {{whereToBuy.tvName}} page, then the soundbar it goes with, the {{whereToBuy.pickupName}}, and chooses Best Buy pickup: an OH order, handed over by a partner
Opens the wall mount the TV goes with, the {{whereToBuy.referralName}}, sold through retailers: Find a Retailer, then {{whereToBuy.retailerName}}
Builds today’s report
will: Each press goes on the wire as a named outcome, partner_pickup and retailer_referral, with the decision on screen that earned it
The day report counts both beside the orders and the attach, labelled attribution, and says not yet significant
beats.line: Best Buy pickup on one page, Find a Retailer on another, and the day report counts both as named outcomes, with attach and attribution. Not yet significant, and it says so: attribution, not incrementality.

after.line: Today’s report: {{report.pickups}} Best Buy pickup(s) and {{report.referrals}} retailer referral(s), each credited to the decision that earned it, beside {{report.orders || 'no'}} order(s) shipped and the attach. Not yet significant: attribution, not incrementality; lift is LG’s to compute against a holdout.
